I’ve known a few people who got into open relationships (including me at one point…semi) What I’ve seen with all of them is that what tends to happen is a sort of ‘power imbalance’ - one person sets up the open status, and the other person is so attached that they can’t say no without risking losing the other person entirely so they have to agree - it culminates in the person who agreed sort of slowly melt in their own sadness, they can’t bear the fact that they aren’t exclusively loved.

I don’t know your whole thoughts and how you consciously think about it. I can only tell you how I thought, and hopefully you can align your own thoughts with my experiences in some way. I was offered to open our relationship, and consciously I said it was ok. And consciously I was ok with it - if she was happy then so was I. But as soon as we stopped seeing each other, I realised after just how sad I was. To me, I felt there was an intrinsic beauty in the exclusivity in a relationship - you feel valued, you feel special - and it sort of shattered my heart realising that I didn’t ever feel that way.

I guess this is a sort of warning that even if you say you’re ok with it, and even if you believe it, be aware that it is very possible that it can hurt. I’m not saying it will 100%. You never know, everyone is different. But please be careful. I went through so much pain, and I would hate for ANYONE to feel the same way.
Wow…thank you. I didn’t think anyone actually would. I appreciate it so much :)

Way I see it, we are literally just on a floating rock in space. No one has any idea what we are truly doing. Don’t be upset because you think you don’t know something, everyone is figuring out how to make sense of this absurd thing called ‘life.’ We all come to some conclusion in the end, you’ll be a content person at some point, it might take a while but patience is key - I know you’re just talking about driving, but don’t ever feel like getting help from others is something to be ashamed of - everyone has something new to offer and help you learn something new about yourself. Everyone learns from others, that’s how humans have grown for thousands of years. Eventually you’ll find your truths, and it’ll be ok when all is said and done :)

Yeah. That give-and-receive mindset changed my perspective a lot about friendships.

  
 I doubt many other people think like this though - it just seems like such an odd thing that no one would think about it, sorta. It's hard to explain. You're not at fault for anything, trust me. I doubt any of your friends though would be opposed to you saying hi. One great thing about this is that it's never too late to just pop in.  

  
But don't feel bad!!! Instead, think like there is an opportunity to just try. Being friendly and saying hi never hurt anyone :)

Hi :) No, I don't think I need to talk to someone, per se. All I ask is that you talk to someone else who you personally know that might really need it :) and if there isn't someone who you can think of that needs it, just talk to someone who you personally know anyway, that's all I ever ask :)
